# v0.49.44

This patch stops Magic Context from rebuilding the cached prompt only because the provider's cache expired, removes a long stall on OpenCode, and fixes a missed rebuild after a restart.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Changed

- **An expired provider cache no longer triggers a rebuild:** when the provider's prompt cache had expired (by default after 5 minutes idle), Magic Context treated the next turn as a free moment to rebuild the prompt: it removed the outputs the agent had marked with `ctx_reduce`, ran cleanup, and folded older history into the summary block. Resending the same request after an expiry already costs one full cache write, and a rebuild at that moment also discarded the model's kept reasoning on Claude models and dropped context the agent might still need well before the context was full. Now an expiry changes nothing: the next turn sends the same bytes. Marked outputs are removed and cleanup runs when usage reaches the execute threshold (65% by default), or on a model or system prompt change, as before. `cache_ttl` no longer triggers any rebuild; it is kept for diagnostics.
- **The date in the system prompt now changes only on a real rebuild:** before, an expired cache let the frozen date move to today, which could fold the prompt at low usage. The date now stays frozen until the prompt is rebuilt for another reason.
- **Providers that report no token usage get pressure handling:** for a provider that sends no usage figures, the expired-cache rebuild was the only time queued drops ever landed. Magic Context now estimates the size of the request it sent and uses that estimate to decide when the execute threshold is reached. An estimate counts as force-band pressure (emergency tool drops) only at 95% or more.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode could stall for seconds while moving the compaction marker:** on long OpenCode sessions, writing the compaction marker scanned the whole session on the main thread, and a pass could wait 20 seconds or more for it. The scan now runs in the background, and a pass never waits for it; the marker moves on a later pass when the scan is ready.
- **The first turn after a restart could rebuild twice:** after a host restart, Magic Context discarded the last usage reading on its first pass. A session that was already over the execute threshold deferred its owed rebuild by one turn, so a cold cache was written twice. The first pass now uses the saved reading to decide whether to run its rebuild, when the reading is for the same model and context size. Other checks on that pass still ignore it. Thanks to @iceteaSA for the report (#882).
- **Docs:** the dreamer page now says the dreamer only runs for projects that a running host has open (#883).

# v0.49.43

This patch makes a refused turn on Pi and Oh My Pi actually stop before it reaches the provider, and lets Oh My Pi's Cursor provider work with Magic Context.

## Upgrading

- Restart Pi or Oh My Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **A refused turn on Pi or Oh My Pi could still reach the model:** when Magic Context refused to send a turn (for example "Magic Context could not safely prepare this turn"), Pi and Oh My Pi still sent the original request. The model answered, its tool calls ran, and the reply was then discarded as aborted. A refused turn is now stopped before anything is sent, no tools run, and the refusal message is shown. The next turn works normally.
- **Every Cursor turn on Oh My Pi was refused:** Magic Context couldn't read the request format of Oh My Pi's Cursor provider (`cursor-agent`), so it refused every turn. It now understands that format, including Cursor's content-addressed history, and checks Cursor turns the same way as other providers. This is checked against Oh My Pi 18.13.2, 18.18.0 and 18.18.1. When a request format isn't recognized, the refusal now names the provider and format, so it's easy to report. Thanks to @Zireael for the detailed report (#880) and the proposed Cursor fix (#881), which we used to check the adapter against Oh My Pi 18.18.

# v0.49.42

This patch stops superseded tool instructions from filling the context window on OpenCode 2.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2 kept sending obsolete Code Mode catalogs:** restarting OpenCode or changing the available tools could leave dozens of old instruction updates in every request, consuming most of the context window before a host compaction ran. Magic Context now removes superseded instruction rows on a pass that is already rebuilding the prompt cache, including rebuilds triggered by high context usage. Each source must have a newer full restatement before its old row can go: incremental Code Mode updates, MCP guidance deltas, and unknown instruction sources stay. The decision survives restarts. On models whose reasoning signatures depend on the preceding conversation, removing a row also removes reasoning blocks invalidated by that edit. Manual compaction uses the same per-source rule. Thanks to @dhaern for the detailed report (#879).

# v0.49.41

This patch removes multi-second pauses on long OpenCode 1 sessions when Magic Context moves OpenCode's compaction marker.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Long OpenCode 1 sessions paused for seconds when history was folded:** since 0.49.36, moving OpenCode's compaction marker first checked the whole session for a row that still pointed at the old marker, and it did that while holding OpenCode's database write lock. On a long session that check took 10 to 30 seconds. The turn waited that long, and so did every other session on the same OpenCode server that tried to write. The check now runs before the lock, on a separate read-only connection, and on later moves it reads only compaction rows and rows written since the previous move. Under the lock, Magic Context rereads just those rows to confirm nothing changed. The protection added in 0.49.36 is unchanged: a marker that OpenCode's own compaction still points at is never deleted.

# v0.49.40

This patch fixes history compaction on OpenCode 2 for sessions that used tools before their first summary.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2 stopped compacting history after a session's first summary:** once a session had a summary that covered tool calls, every turn logged `v3 host fold: capture unavailable: Error: Native carrier has no source row coordinate`. From then on, Magic Context couldn't fold history into OpenCode 2's own compaction for that session, and a later compaction refused the turn with `Manual compaction controls have not been captured`. OpenCode 2 sends tool results without a message id, and a tool result whose call was already summarized was kept on its own, with no message to attach it to. A tool result now stays or goes together with the message that made its call, in the same step that attaches messages to OpenCode's stored rows. Sessions affected before the update recover on their next turn. Thanks to @botbeech for the precise report and reproduction (#875).
